subsystems.name: Growth environment
subsystems.role: provides stacked, controlled conditions for plant growth without soil.

subsystems.name: Plant chassis
subsystems.role: the engineered plant that acts as a living factory for the target protein.

subsystems.name: Genetic engineering toolkit
subsystems.role: introduces and controls the genes that make the desired protein.

subsystems.name: Bioprocessing
subsystems.role: harvests plant material and extracts and purifies the protein.

subsystems.name: Automation and monitoring
subsystems.role: keeps the vertical farm running reliably and at low labour cost.
parts: software for climate and fertigation control

subsystems.name: Containment
subsystems.role: prevents engineered plants or their genes from escaping into the environment.

buildSteps.title: Select and engineer the plant chassis
buildSteps.detail: Choose a fast-growing, easily transformed species. Insert genes for the target protein using CRISPR or other methods, with promoters that allow controlled expression.

buildSteps.title: Establish sterile cultures
buildSteps.detail: Regenerate transformed plantlets or seeds under sterile conditions to ensure a uniform, contamination-free starting material.

buildSteps.title: Scale up in vertical hydroponic racks
buildSteps.detail: Move plantlets into stacked trays with recirculating nutrient solution, LED lighting tuned to the plant’s needs, and controlled temperature, humidity and CO2.

buildSteps.title: Induce protein production
buildSteps.detail: Trigger the promoter (e.g., with a chemical or a change in light) so the plants begin making the target protein. Monitor expression levels.

buildSteps.title: Harvest biomass
buildSteps.detail: Collect leaves or whole plants at peak expression, using automated cutting and transport to keep the material fresh.

buildSteps.title: Extract and purify
buildSteps.detail: Homogenise the biomass, clarify the liquid, and use chromatography or other separation steps to isolate the protein to the required purity.

buildSteps.title: Quality control
buildSteps.detail: Test for identity, potency, and absence of toxins, pesticides or microbial contamination. For pharmaceuticals, follow good manufacturing practice.

buildSteps.title: Package and distribute
buildSteps.detail: Formulate the protein for its final use—as a drug, a food ingredient, or an input for cultivated meat—and ship under appropriate conditions.

prerequisites.why: decades of research allow reliable transformation and expression of foreign proteins in plants.
commercial vertical farms already grow leafy greens indoors at scale, proving the growth environment.
methods to extract and purify proteins from plant material are well established in the biotech industry.
some plant-made pharmaceuticals are approved, but rules for vertical-grown food proteins and novel ingredients are still developing.
vertical farming is energy-intensive and currently cheaper for high-value pharmaceuticals than for commodity food proteins.

pathway.milestone: research and clinical-scale production of high-value proteins in contained vertical systems
pathway.unlocks: proof that plants can make complex proteins with the right quality attributes.

pathway.milestone: pilot plants producing a small number of approved pharmaceuticals or food ingredients
pathway.unlocks: real cost and regulatory data for vertical molecular farming.

pathway.milestone: on-site production of growth factors and other inputs for cultivated meat
pathway.unlocks: a cheaper, more resilient supply chain for the cultivated-meat industry.

pathway.milestone: decentralised vertical molecular farms making multiple products
pathway.unlocks: local production of medicines and food ingredients, reducing dependence on long supply chains.
